core: setting as time, place, and environment
supporting: setting's relation to plot and characterization

claims.claim: Setting is a meaningful narrative arrangement of environments in which events occur and can include time, place, and material conditions.
Topographical details present spatial or material arrangement, while atmosphere concerns meaningful relations between environment and experience.
Setting may support plot and characterization, provide a character-centered experience of place, or become symbolic through a supported relation to other story elements.
Description selects details that can orient readers, establish a sense of plausibility, and connect environments to events or characters.
A setting analysis should connect details to narrative consequences and not assume that one image has an invariant symbolic meaning.
A fictional representation of a place is perspective-bound and should not be treated as a complete report about a real community.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Introductory resources define setting narrowly as time and place or more broadly as the arrangement of environments and experience.
positions: One source gives a concise time-and-place definition.
One source develops setting through topography, atmosphere, narrative function, and representation.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson starts with time and place, then treats material and social conditions as relevant when the text makes them meaningful.
